To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the poloidal impurity-density variation can change from being always inboardward in the Pfirsch-Schluther and banana regimes to having the same probability of being either inboardward or outboardward in the plateau regime, and that the impurity flow is modified relative to neoclassical predictions in all regimes.
in a tokamak plasma with plateau-regime ions, the density of an impurity can be higher at the in-board side, and the poloidal variation in its velocity is modified.
impurity density is higher at either the inner or outer side of the pedestal in the plateau regime and the impurity flow is modified relative to conventional neoclassically calculated results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the poloidal variation of impurity density in the pedestal region of a tokamak.
the radial and poloidal structure of impurities in the pedestal of a high-confinement-mode (H-mode) tokamak.
the poloidal variation in density of impurity species in the edge of a tokamak.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the poloidal variation of impurities depends on the collisionality of the main ions, and that the impurity flows are always modified relative to the neoclassical prediction.
the poloidal variation of the impurity density in the pedestal is a complicated function of the collisionality, rotation, and the impurity mass, charge, and temperature.

in the plateau regime the impurity density profile can be either peaked or hollow, and that the poloidal variation of the density can be either outboard- or inboard-peaked, depending on the magnitude and direction of the impurity flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impurity flows and density are modified by the main-ion rotation and collisionality in a nontrivial way.
the impurity poloidal density variation and flow are determined by the collisionalities and temperatures of the main ions and the impurity species.
the impurity flow is modified in a similar way to the main-ion flow, except that there are additional terms that depend on the poloidal density variation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the poloidal density variation of an impurity is not a reliable indicator of the poloidal rotation of the main ions.
the poloidal variation in impurity density can have a significant influence on the pedestal width.
the poloidal variation in impurity density and flow can be different in the pedestal of a rotating tokamak from that in a nonrotating tokamak.
